builtins.name: adsr
builtins.doc: Gated ADSR envelope. Rises while the gate is positive, releases when it returns to zero. Times are in seconds; sustain is a level in 0..=1.

builtins.name: afollow
builtins.doc: Asymmetric parameter follower. Smooths rising segments over `attack` and falling ones over `release` (halfway response times, in seconds).

builtins.name: allpass
builtins.doc: Allpass filter. Passes all frequencies but shifts their phase around the center frequency.

builtins.name: allpole
builtins.doc: First-order allpass filter with a configurable delay at DC, in samples (must be > 0).

builtins.name: bandpass
builtins.doc: Bandpass filter. Keeps frequencies near the center, attenuating either side.

builtins.name: bandrez
builtins.doc: Resonant two-pole bandpass filter.

builtins.name: bell
builtins.doc: Bell equalizer. Boosts or cuts a band around the center frequency by `gain` (an amplitude multiplier, not dB).

builtins.name: biquad
builtins.doc: Arbitrary biquad filter with coefficients in normalized form. All five coefficients must be constants.

builtins.name: brown
builtins.doc: Brown noise: -6 dB per octave. Darker than pink.

builtins.name: butterpass
builtins.doc: Second-order Butterworth lowpass. Maximally flat passband, no resonance control.

builtins.name: chorus
builtins.doc: Five-voice mono chorus, mixed with the dry signal. Stack two with different seeds for stereo. All parameters except the audio input are constants.

builtins.name: clip
builtins.doc: Hard-clip the signal to -1..=1.

builtins.name: clip_to
builtins.doc: Hard-clip the signal to `minimum`..=`maximum`. Both bounds are constants.

builtins.name: dcblock
builtins.doc: Remove DC offset, keeping the signal zero-centered. Cutoff is 10 Hz.

builtins.name: declick
builtins.doc: Fade the signal in over 10 ms from time zero, suppressing the click at the start of a graph.

builtins.name: delay
builtins.doc: Fixed delay of `time` seconds, rounded to the nearest sample. The time is a constant — use `tap` for a modulatable delay.

builtins.name: dsf_saw
builtins.doc: Saw-like discrete summation formula oscillator. `roughness` in 0..=1 sets how much successive partials are attenuated.

builtins.name: env
builtins.doc: Time-based ADSR for one-shot voices. Attack, decay and sustain fill `duration`; the release starts where that ends and rings on for its own time past it, so the note is held for `duration` and the voice lasts `duration + release`. Pass the voice-bound `dur` as the duration — `legato` shortens the held part and leaves the release alone. All arguments are constants.

builtins.name: dsf_square
builtins.doc: Square-like discrete summation formula oscillator. `roughness` in 0..=1 sets how much successive partials are attenuated.

builtins.name: fir3
builtins.doc: Three-point symmetric FIR filter, specified by its `gain` (>= 0) at the Nyquist frequency. A gain below 1 gives a gentle lowpass.

builtins.name: follow
builtins.doc: Parameter follower. Smooths the signal with the given halfway response time, in seconds.

builtins.name: hammond
builtins.doc: Hammond organ wavetable oscillator. Emphasizes the first three partials.

builtins.name: highpass
builtins.doc: Resonant highpass filter.

builtins.name: highpole
builtins.doc: First-order one-pole one-zero highpass. No resonance.

builtins.name: highshelf
builtins.doc: High shelf filter. Scales everything above the center frequency by `gain` (an amplitude multiplier).

builtins.name: hold
builtins.doc: Sample-and-hold. Samples the signal at `frequency` Hz; `variability` in 0..=1 jitters the sampling interval and is a constant.

builtins.name: impulse
builtins.doc: A single one followed by silence. Useful for exciting `pluck` or measuring an impulse response.

builtins.name: limiter
builtins.doc: Look-ahead limiter holding the signal to -1..=1. Look-ahead equals the attack time. Times are constants, in seconds.

builtins.name: line
builtins.doc: One straight segment: `start` to `end` over `duration` seconds, held at `end` after that. Measured from the onset — the note's in a voice, the eval's in the persistent graph — so it needs no note length and works in either: `sin(line(880, 220, 0.05))` is a kick's pitch drop. Unlike `perc` it ends at a level rather than at silence, so it holds a voice open past its note only when `end` is 0 and the shape really finishes. All three arguments are constants; for a sweep between signals, scale it — `start + (end - start) * line(0, 1, d)`.

builtins.name: lorenz
builtins.doc: Lorenz chaotic oscillator. The frequency input has only a slight effect on the output.

builtins.name: lowpass
builtins.doc: Resonant lowpass filter.

builtins.name: lowpole
builtins.doc: First-order one-pole lowpass. No resonance.

builtins.name: lowrez
builtins.doc: Resonant two-pole lowpass filter.

builtins.name: lowshelf
builtins.doc: Low shelf filter. Scales everything below the center frequency by `gain` (an amplitude multiplier).

builtins.name: mls
builtins.doc: Maximum length sequence noise: a repeating pseudorandom run of -1 and 1.

builtins.name: mls_bits
builtins.doc: Maximum length sequence noise from an n-bit sequence (1..=31). More bits means a longer period before it repeats. Constant.

builtins.name: moog
builtins.doc: Moog-style resonant lowpass ladder filter.

builtins.name: morph
builtins.doc: Filter that morphs continuously between modes: `morph` runs -1 (lowpass) to 0 (peak) to 1 (highpass).

builtins.name: noise
builtins.doc: White noise.

builtins.name: notch
builtins.doc: Notch filter. Removes a narrow band around the center frequency.

builtins.name: organ
builtins.doc: Organ wavetable oscillator. Emphasizes octave partials.

builtins.name: peak
builtins.doc: Peaking filter.

builtins.name: perc
builtins.doc: Self-contained percussive envelope: rise, fall, silence. Needs no note length, so it works in a voice or the persistent graph — and in a voice the shape is measured from the onset and always finishes, so a drum longer than the step it sits on rings on into the next rather than being cut off. Both times are constants.

builtins.name: pink
builtins.doc: Pink noise: -3 dB per octave.

builtins.name: pinkpass
builtins.doc: Pinking filter: -3 dB per octave. Turns white noise into pink.

builtins.name: pluck
builtins.doc: Karplus-Strong plucked string. Feed it a burst — `impulse()` or a short noise envelope — as the excitation. Frequency, gain and damping (0..=1) are constants.

builtins.name: poly_pulse
builtins.doc: PolyBLEP pulse wave. Fast and fairly bandlimited; `width` in 0..=1 is the duty cycle.

builtins.name: poly_saw
builtins.doc: PolyBLEP saw wave. Fast and fairly bandlimited.

builtins.name: poly_square
builtins.doc: PolyBLEP square wave. Fast and fairly bandlimited.

builtins.name: pulse
builtins.doc: Bandlimited pulse wave oscillator. `width` in 0..=1 is the duty cycle.

builtins.name: ramp
builtins.doc: Rising ramp from 0 to 1 at the given repetition frequency, starting at 0. Not bandlimited — useful as a phasor, not as audio. Its zero is the start of its own period, which is what lets it drive `sample`: `sample(b, ramp(1 / b.secs))` reads a buffer once, end to end.

builtins.name: resonator
builtins.doc: Constant-gain bandpass resonator.

builtins.name: reverb
builtins.doc: Reverb (32-channel FDN). `room_size` is in meters (10 is an average room), `time` is the decay to -60 dB in seconds, `damping` in 0..=1 rolls off the highs. Wet only: `x + reverb(x, 10, 3, 0.5) * 0.2`. All parameters except the audio input are constants.

builtins.name: reverb2
builtins.doc: Hybrid FDN reverb — richer and more expensive than `reverb`. `room_size` is in meters and clamps to 10..=30, `diffusion` in 0..=1 thickens the tail, `modulation` around 1 adds movement (higher goes audibly Doppler), and `damping_cutoff` is the lowpass applied to each loop pass, in hertz. Wet only. All parameters except the audio input are constants.

builtins.name: reverb3
builtins.doc: Allpass-loop reverb, with no room size — just `time` to -60 dB, `diffusion` in 0..=1, and a `damping_cutoff` in hertz applied to each loop pass. Wet only. All parameters except the audio input are constants.

builtins.name: reverb4
builtins.doc: Reverb with a slow fade-in, for swells rather than rooms. `room_size` is in meters and is treated as at least 15; below that the delay times stop sounding like a space. Wet only. Both `room_size` and `time` are constants.

builtins.name: rossler
builtins.doc: Rossler chaotic oscillator, with peaks at multiples of the frequency input.

builtins.name: saw
builtins.doc: Bandlimited saw wavetable oscillator.

builtins.name: sin
builtins.doc: Sine oscillator.

builtins.name: soft_saw
builtins.doc: Soft saw wavetable oscillator. Contains all partials but falls off like a triangle wave.

builtins.name: square
builtins.doc: Bandlimited square wavetable oscillator.

builtins.name: tap
builtins.doc: Tapped delay line with cubic interpolation. Unlike `delay`, the delay time is a signal, so it can be modulated — it must stay within the constant `min_delay`..=`max_delay` bounds, in seconds.

builtins.name: tick
builtins.doc: Single-sample delay. The building block for feedback and comb filters.

builtins.name: triangle
builtins.doc: Bandlimited triangle wavetable oscillator.

builtins.name: len
builtins.doc: The number of elements in the list.

builtins.name: zip
builtins.doc: Pair elements positionally: `zip([1, 2], [3, 4])` is `[[1, 3], [2, 4]]`. Every argument must be a list, and all must be the same length.

builtins.name: stack
builtins.doc: Patterns that sound at once instead of in turn: `stack([c4;2, e4;2], [g4;4])` is a two-note line under a held g. Each argument keeps its own division, so the layers need not agree on a rhythm — a three against a four is written by stacking them. This is how a chord is written, and how a drawn part with overlapping notes is split into voices. Lanes read a stack as all its values in order, layer by layer.

builtins.name: rev
builtins.doc: The list, back to front.

builtins.name: palindrome
builtins.doc: The list followed by its mirror: `[a, b, c]` becomes `[a, b, c, c, b, a]`.

builtins.name: rotl
builtins.doc: Rotate left, wrapping. `amount` defaults to 1; a negative amount rotates right.

builtins.name: rotr
builtins.doc: Rotate right, wrapping. `amount` defaults to 1; a negative amount rotates left.

builtins.name: push
builtins.doc: A new list with `value` appended. Lists are immutable — the original is unchanged.

builtins.name: pop
builtins.doc: A new list without its last element. Index the list to read that element.

builtins.name: sort
builtins.doc: The list sorted ascending. Every element must be a compile-time number.

builtins.name: sum
builtins.doc: Add every element together. Folds numbers at compile time and emits mixing nodes for signals, so a list of oscillators sums into the graph.

builtins.name: split
builtins.doc: Break the list into chunks of `size`. A short final chunk is kept.

builtins.name: choice
builtins.doc: One element picked at random. Re-rolled on every eval.

builtins.name: wchoice
builtins.doc: One element picked at random, weighted. The two lists run in parallel; weights must be finite and >= 0.

builtins.name: scramble
builtins.doc: The list shuffled. Re-rolled on every eval.

builtins.name: map
builtins.doc: Apply a function to every element: `riff.map(up)`. The transform is an ordinary user `fn` of one argument, and may answer with anything — mapping to oscillators is the only way to hold several voices apart, since a `for` over audio sums instead of collecting.

builtins.name: dot
builtins.doc: Dot a written note value: `q.dot` is a dotted quarter, a quarter and an eighth. `dots` defaults to 1; `q.dot(2)` is the doubly-dotted quarter, which is a quarter and an eighth and a sixteenth. Written as a count rather than by repeating `.dot`, because each dot adds half of the note itself rather than half of what the last one left.

builtins.name: filter
builtins.doc: Keep the elements the predicate answers non-zero for. The predicate is an ordinary user `fn` of one argument.

builtins.name: m2h
builtins.doc: MIDI note number to frequency in hertz: `69.m2h` is 440. Equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz.

builtins.name: h2m
builtins.doc: Frequency in hertz to MIDI note number, the inverse of `m2h`: `440.h2m` is 69. The result may be fractional.

builtins.name: db
builtins.doc: Decibels to a linear amplitude: `0.db` is 1, `-6.db` is about 0.5. Use it to write gains the way you hear them.

builtins.name: amp
builtins.doc: Linear amplitude to decibels, the inverse of `db`: `1.amp` is 0. The amplitude must be above zero.

builtins.name: cents
builtins.doc: Detune a frequency by cents, 1/100 of a semitone: `440.cents(-14)` flattens A4 slightly.

builtins.name: bpm
builtins.doc: Beats per minute to bars per second. The beat is the quarter note; how many of them make a bar is the project's time signature, so `120.bpm` is 0.5 in 4/4 — the default tempo — and 0.667 in 3/4, where the bar is shorter.

builtins.name: oct
builtins.doc: Transpose a MIDI note by whole octaves: `60.oct(-1)` is 48.

builtins.name: semi
builtins.doc: Transpose a MIDI note by semitones: `60.semi(7)` is 67.

builtins.name: scale
builtins.doc: Snap a MIDI note to the nearest tone of a scale, given as semitone offsets within an octave: `61.scale([0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11])` is 60. Ties snap down.

builtins.name: clamp
builtins.doc: Constrain a number to `lo..=hi`.

builtins.name: norm
builtins.doc: Map 0..1 onto `lo..hi`. Values outside 0..1 extrapolate; `clamp` first if you do not want that.

builtins.name: wrap
builtins.doc: Fold a number back into `lo..hi`, wrapping around rather than clamping. Useful for modular pitch.

builtins.name: round
builtins.doc: Nearest whole number, halves away from zero.

builtins.name: floor
builtins.doc: Largest whole number at or below `x`.

builtins.name: ceil
builtins.doc: Smallest whole number at or above `x`.

builtins.name: abs
builtins.doc: Magnitude, dropping the sign.

builtins.name: pow
builtins.doc: `x` raised to a power: `2.pow(10)` is 1024. Good for exponential curve shaping.

builtins.name: sqrt
builtins.doc: Square root. `x` must not be negative.

builtins.name: log2
builtins.doc: Base-2 logarithm. `x` must be above zero.

builtins.name: rand
builtins.doc: A uniform number. `rand()` draws from 0..1; `rand(lo, hi)` — or `60.rand(72)` — draws from `lo..hi`, with `hi` excluded.

builtins.name: randi
builtins.doc: A uniform whole number in `lo..hi`, with `hi` excluded: `randi(60, 72)` is an octave of notes that never repeats the root. Both bounds must be whole.

builtins.name: coin
builtins.doc: 1 or 0, at odds you choose. `coin()` is even; `coin(0.25)` answers 1 one time in four. Multiply by it to drop a note, or add it to a velocity.

builtins.name: seed
builtins.doc: Fix every draw made after it, and answer with the seed. `seed(42)` at the top of a program makes its lists, lanes and patterns come out the same on every evaluation — which is how a happy accident gets kept. A voice is lowered per note and does not see a top-level seed, so a `seed` inside an instrument pins that instrument instead, identically on every note.

builtins.name: gauss
builtins.doc: A normally distributed number: clustered around `mean`, two thirds of it within one `deviation`. Both default to the standard 0 and 1. Unbounded — `clamp` it if a stray value would hurt.

builtins.name: humanize
builtins.doc: Nudge a number off its grid: `x` plus a normal draw of deviation `amount`, so most nudges are small and a few are not. `0.5.humanize(0.05)` is a velocity that no longer sounds typed in.

builtins.name: expo
builtins.doc: An exponentially distributed number above zero with the given `mean` (default 1). Short values are common and long ones rare — the shape of a wait between events.

builtins.name: tri
builtins.doc: A triangular draw over `lo..hi`, peaking at `mode` — the midpoint if you leave it out. Bounded like `rand` but with a centre, so it favours a value without ever leaving the range.

builtins.name: cauchy
builtins.doc: A heavy-tailed draw around `median` (default 0) with the given `spread` (default 1). Mostly close in, but far more prone to a wild outlier than `gauss` — which is the point when you want the occasional lurch.

builtins.name: pareto
builtins.doc: A power-law draw at or above `scale` (default 1). A smaller `shape` (default 1) makes big values likelier. Everything is near the floor, with rare excursions far above it.

builtins.name: poisson
builtins.doc: A whole count averaging `mean` (default 1) — how many things happened, when each was independent. Good for deciding how many hits land in a bar.

builtins.name: rands
builtins.doc: A list of `count` uniform numbers, from 0..1 or from `lo..hi`. A pattern in one line: `rands(8, 0.2, 0.9)` is eight velocities.

builtins.name: randis
builtins.doc: A list of `count` whole numbers in `lo..hi`, `hi` excluded: `randis(8, 60, 72) >> play(lead)` is an eight-note riff.

builtins.name: walk
builtins.doc: A random walk: `count` numbers beginning at `start`, each drifting from the one before by up to `step` either way. Neighbours stay close, so it moves rather than jumps — what `rands` is not. Good for a cutoff or a pan.

builtins.name: walki
builtins.doc: `walk` in whole steps: each move is a whole number from `-step` to `step`, so the result stays on the semitone grid. `walki(16, 60, 2)` wanders a melody around middle C. `step` must be whole.

builtins.name: choices
builtins.doc: `count` elements drawn without replacement, in a random order — `choice` several times over may repeat itself, and this cannot. Asking for the whole list is `scramble`; asking for more than it holds is an error.

builtins.name: randscale
builtins.doc: `count` notes drawn evenly from the tones of a scale, given as semitone offsets within an octave, between MIDI `lo` and `hi` (60..72 by default). Unlike snapping a uniform draw with `scale`, every degree is equally likely and nothing lands outside the range: `randscale(8, [0, 3, 5, 7, 10], 48, 72)` is a pentatonic riff over two octaves.

builtins.name: then
builtins.doc: Sequence one section after another: `playn(verse, lead, 4).then(chorus)`. The left side must be `play_once` or `playn` — plain `play` never finishes. `section` is either a no-parameter `fn` named here or a play written out — `.then(playn(riff, lead, 2))` needs no name — and either way its own `play` calls start where this one stops. A play bound to a `let` is not a section: it already sounded where it was written, so name it as a `fn` instead. Lowered at eval time, not called by the audio thread.

builtins.name: then_after
builtins.doc: `then`, with `bars` of silence in between: `playn(verse, lead, 4).then_after(1, chorus)` leaves a bar's rest before the chorus. The gap cannot be negative — `overlap` is how a section starts early.

builtins.name: overlap
builtins.doc: `then`, but the section starts `bars` *before* this one ends, so the two really do sound together over the join: `playn(verse, lead, 8).overlap(2, chorus)`. Never earlier than the receiver's own start. The chain carries on from whichever of the two ends later.

builtins.name: with
builtins.doc: Run a section *alongside* this one, from where it began: `playn(verse, lead, 4).with(drums).then(chorus)`. `play_all` opens its sections together as a group; this makes one concurrent with a section already placed, so an arrangement reads in the order it happens. The pair finishes when the later of them does.

builtins.name: at
builtins.doc: Place a section at an absolute bar, counted from the origin: `at(8, chorus)`. Bars are counted from 0, so `at(8, …)` is the ninth bar — it is a distance from the start, the same number `then_after` would have added up to. The escape hatch from chaining, for an arrangement whose shape you already know.

builtins.name: seq
builtins.doc: Sections one after another without the nesting: `seq(intro, verse, chorus, verse)`. Each is a no-parameter `fn` or a play written out, and each must finish for the next to follow.

builtins.name: then_n
builtins.doc: Run a section `times` times, back to back: `play_once(intro, lead).then_n(verse, 4)`. Lowered afresh each pass rather than written once and repeated, so a `rand` inside the section is a different number every time round — the same rule a voice already follows, and it holds whether the section is a `fn` named here or a play written out.

builtins.name: loop
builtins.doc: Everything chained so far, `times` times through: `playn(groove, kit, 3).then_fill(roll).loop(4)` is four bars of groove-and-fill. The counterpart to `then_n` — that one names a `fn` and runs it *after* this section, this one takes no section at all because the section it repeats is the chain it is written on. The whole chain has to finish, so bound an endless part with `.take(n)` or `.stop()` first. The passes are copies, so a `rand` inside the chain was already spent and every pass is the same music; `then_n` is the one that draws afresh.

builtins.name: then_each
builtins.doc: One pass of the section per element of the list, in sequence, with the element passed in: `play_once(intro, lead).then_each([1, 2, 4], faster)` calls `faster(1)`, then `faster(2)`, then `faster(4)`. `body` takes exactly one parameter — the element. Arrangement by list — every list function in the language already builds the shape of a piece, and this is what spends one. Unlike `then`, the sections here must be `fn`s named rather than plays written out: this runs one afresh rather than placing it once.

builtins.name: then_fill
builtins.doc: One pass of a pattern on this section's *own* instrument: `playn(groove, drums, 4).then_fill([1, 1, 1, 1])`. Unlike `then` there is no `fn` and no second `play` — a fill is played by whoever just played, so the instrument and every lane are inherited and only the pattern is new. The left side has to be a single `play`: a group of them has no one instrument to be a fill for. `rate` defaults to 1, and here is a plain number — a fill is one pass, with no room to speed up over.

builtins.name: quantize
builtins.doc: Round where the chain has reached up to a multiple of `grid` bars, without touching what is already playing: `playn(pat, inst, 3, 2).quantize().then(chorus)`. `grid` defaults to 1. The cure for a section whose length is not a whole number of bars — `rate` divides into the count, so `playn(pat, inst, 3, 2)` is 1.5 bars long and every `.then` after it would otherwise be permanently off the downbeat.

builtins.name: take
builtins.doc: This section, cut to `bars`: `play(riff, lead).take(8).then(chorus)`. What gives a plain `play` an end — `playn` only bounds a single play, not a `play_all` group or a whole nested section. A part that already stops sooner is left alone, since a cut is a ceiling and not a length.

builtins.name: stop
builtins.doc: Cut everything still open in this section at the moment its last *counted* part finishes: `play_all(play(groove, drums), playn(riff, lead, 8)).stop()` lets the eight-bar riff decide when the endless drums give up. One pattern as the trigger to stop the rest. Needs at least one `play_once` or `playn` among them, or there is no moment to stop at.

builtins.name: wthen
builtins.doc: Choose between sections, afresh each time round: `playn(intro, lead, 2).wthen([verse, chorus], [0.7, 0.3])`. Weights are relative and need not sum to 1. Unlike `choice`, which draws once while the program is lowered, this is decided by the scheduler as the music reaches it — so the block repeats forever and deals a new hand every time. Every arm must finish, and they all come back to the same place; the block itself never finishes, so bound it with `.take(n)` if something should follow. Unlike `then`, the sections here must be `fn`s named rather than plays written out: this runs one afresh rather than placing it once.

builtins.name: rthen
builtins.doc: `wthen` with every section equally likely: `playn(intro, lead, 2).rthen([verse, chorus, bridge])`. Rerolls each time round and never finishes, exactly as `wthen` does. Unlike `then`, the sections here must be `fn`s named rather than plays written out: this runs one afresh rather than placing it once.

builtins.name: maybe
builtins.doc: Play a section with probability `chance` (0 to 1), decided afresh each time round: `playn(groove, drums, 4).maybe(0.25, fill)`. A `wthen` whose other arm is silence — it repeats and rerolls for the same reason, since a coin flipped once is just an `if`. Unlike `then`, the sections here must be `fn`s named rather than plays written out: this runs one afresh rather than placing it once.

builtins.name: shuffle_then
builtins.doc: Every section once each, in an order drawn now: `play_once(intro, lead).shuffle_then([verse, chorus, bridge])`. The counterpart to `rthen` rather than a variant of it — a weighted choice may pass a section over for a long time, and this cannot. It settles at eval time like `scramble`, so it has a length and a `.then` may follow it. Unlike `then`, the sections here must be `fn`s named rather than plays written out: this runs one afresh rather than placing it once.

builtins.name: play
builtins.doc: Schedule a pattern on an instrument: `pat >> play(kick)`. The instrument must name a user `fn`. `rate` defaults to 1, and may be an `accel` rather than a number. A list is one pass, filling the bar, divided evenly unless a step is given a length with `;` — `[220;2, 330, 440, `;4]` is a quarter, two eighths and a half of silence — and lengths are relative, so only their ratio matters. A long step is one sustained note, not several. A step may instead be given a written note value — `w` `h` `q` `e` `s` — and then the pass is as long as its values add up to rather than one bar: in 4/4 `[c4;q, e4, g4]` is three beats against a four-beat bar, so it comes round a beat early and rotates against the grid. A value carries to the steps after it. A bare `q` is a hit of that length. An octave carries the same way: a note written without one takes the octave of the last note that spelled one, so `[a1;q, a, a, a]` is four `a1`s and `[c4;q, ef, g]` is a chord's worth of arpeggio. Only a spelled octave moves it, a group gives it back at the closing bracket like a written value does, and `e` — the eighth note and also the note E — is refused where an octave is in force rather than quietly becoming one of them. Written values and ratios cannot share a sequence. A group inside one is a tuplet and says so with `;t` — `[[c4;q, e4, g4];t, c5]` is a quarter triplet then a quarter — which needs no number: the count, the unit and the span it is played in all follow from what the group holds. Any further parameter is patterned by name — `play(bass, cut: [400, 2000])` — sampled at each note's onset, and lanes may be any length. In a lane a `;` is how many notes the value covers, so it has to be a whole number there. Two names are reserved and reach the note rather than the instrument: `legato:` scales its length, and `pan:` places it across the stereo field from -1 (left) through 0 (centre) to 1 (right).

builtins.name: play_once
builtins.doc: `play`, stopping after one pass of the pattern: `[60, 64, 67] >> play_once(stab)`. Started while something is already playing it begins on the next bar, so the one-shot lands on a downbeat. Re-evaluating fires it again.

builtins.name: playn
builtins.doc: `play`, stopping after `times` passes of the pattern: `playn([220, 330], bass, 4)`. `rate` follows the count and still defaults to 1 — at rate 2 the four passes take two bars. Lanes work as they do on `play`.

builtins.name: play_all
builtins.doc: Treat several sections that run at once as one: `play_all(verse, bassline).then(chorus)`. Each is a no-parameter `fn` or a play written out, exactly as in `seq` — the difference is that these all start together rather than one after another, and the group finishes when the last of them does. A plain `play` among them never finishes, so nothing may follow.

builtins.name: accel
builtins.doc: A rate that moves: `from` to `to` over `bars` bars, holding at `to` after that. Written where a `play` takes a number — `playn(riff, lead, 8, accel(1, 2, 4))` runs eight passes, speeding up to double over the first four bars — and it is a straight line in rate, so the pattern covers the area under it rather than the rate at either end. Measured from the section's own first note, and started afresh each time a `wthen` window comes round again. `to` below `from` is a ritardando. Both rates must be above zero: at zero the pattern would stop rather than slow, and a bounded section would never finish.

builtins.name: dur
builtins.doc: The current note's length in seconds. Bound only inside a voice — pass it to `env`.

builtins.name: qvs
builtins.doc: The quarter note in seconds: 0.5 at the default 120 bpm. Anything that takes a length of time can be written in beats with it — `perc(0, qvs / 2)` decays over an eighth, `delay(qvs * 0.75)` is a dotted-eighth delay. Inside a voice it is the beat of the clock that note is played on, so a `play` at rate 2 gives its instrument a beat half as long; in the persistent graph it is the transport's own, fixed at the eval that wrote it.

builtins.name: qvh
builtins.doc: The quarter note in hertz — `1 / qvs`, which is 2 at the default 120 bpm. What an oscillator wants: `sin(qvh * 2)` sweeps on the eighth, `sin(qvh / 2)` on the half. Multiplying is what makes it faster here, because this is a rate and not a length. Rate and tempo reach it exactly as they reach `qvs`.

builtins.name: load
builtins.doc: Read an audio file into a buffer: `let amen = load("breaks/amen.wav")`. The path is relative to the file it is written in, the same way a `use` path is, and must be written out rather than computed — every file is decoded once, before the program runs, so no note ever waits on a disk. Any format symphonia reads: wav, mp3, flac, ogg. Nothing comes out of a buffer until `sample` reads it.

builtins.name: sample
builtins.doc: Read a buffer at a position: 0 is the start, 1 is the end, and anything outside that is silence. `position` is a signal, which is where speed, direction and chopping all come from — `sample(b, ramp(1 / b.secs))` plays it forwards, `1 - ramp(...)` backwards, `ramp(...) * 0.25` reads the first quarter. Cubic interpolation, so it holds up away from its own speed. `channel` defaults to 0 and wraps if the buffer has fewer.

builtins.name: slice
builtins.doc: Read a portion of a buffer, once: `slice(amen, 0, 0.25)` is the first quarter of the break, at the speed it was recorded at. `start` and `end` are positions like `sample`'s, 0 at the start of the buffer and 1 at the end, and both are compile-time numbers rather than signals. `start` past `end` plays that portion backwards. `rate` defaults to 1 and multiplies the speed — 2 reads the portion in half the time, an octave up, 0.5 in twice, an octave down — and must be above zero, since at zero the reader would stop rather than slow; backwards is the ends the other way round rather than a negative rate. This is `sample` with the phasor written for you — `sample(b, line(start, end, (end - start) * b.secs / rate))` — and it exists because that duration is the part that is easy to get wrong: scaling a `ramp`'s position without scaling its frequency to match reads the right portion at the wrong speed. The read holds on the last sample once it arrives, so an envelope is what ends the note, exactly as with `sample`; a slice ending at 1 goes quiet on its own, since past the buffer is silence. For a position or a speed that moves under a signal — scrubbing, stuttering, anything modulated — use `sample`.

builtins.name: secs
builtins.doc: How long a buffer is, in seconds. A compile-time number, so it divides into a `ramp` frequency: `ramp(1 / amen.secs)` is a phasor that reads the whole buffer once at its own speed.

builtins.name: channels
builtins.doc: How many channels a buffer has — 1 for mono, 2 for a stereo file. Useful for deciding whether a second `sample` on channel 1 would say anything different.

durations.name: w
durations.doc: Whole note — four beats, which is one bar in 4/4 and more than one in any shorter meter.

durations.name: s
durations.doc: Sixteenth note — a quarter of a beat.

durations.name: t
durations.doc: Tuplet — play this group in the next lower power of two. Three quarters in the time of two, five eighths in the time of four. Its contents have to fill the division, and cannot already come to a plain duration.
